replies.author: Glittering-Chef-4914
replies.body: thanks for sharing, did you do it a while ago or it still required a lot of iteration with the latest updates? once you figured out the BPM and mood descriptor could you consistently get good music?

replies.author: BSwayzeYo
replies.body:
I did it about 10ish days ago.

The bpm is tricky. If you want slow music you can’t really go lower than about 65bpm. The ai is trained to fill space with sound.

So you also want to include descriptors like… Long notes, no fast runs, deep sonorous instruments, no treble melody.

It still requires a lot of iteration, but the basic suno monthly fee is $9 and you get about 500 created songs.

I recommend not making music with Suno unless you have the subscription, because the license they grant for commercial use does NOT go into retroactive effect. If you make a perfect song and you’re not subscribed, you can’t legally use that track. Ever.
